newsitem.title: FINLAND: U.S. official sees progress but no NATO deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. official sees progress but no NATO deal.

text.p: The United States and Russia made "progress on all fronts" at the Helsinki summit on Friday but agreed to disagree about NATO enlargement, a senior U.S. official said.

The official told Reuters there was agreement on arms control issues. The two sides agreed to disagree on NATO enlargement but they would continue to cooperate, he said, adding: "We have shown we can do business."
"Basically we were able to make progress on all fronts," the official said.

U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin wrapped up their summit talks after two sessions and a working lunch, spending a little over four hours together at Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari's official residence.
Clinton and Yeltsin planned a news conference for 1645 GMT.
The U.S. president returns to Washington later on Friday, while Yeltsin was scheduled to stay on for talks with Ahtisaari on Saturday before flying back to Moscow.
